subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: Should gateway startup keep the current fail-fast SecretRef contract, or should OpenClaw add a bounded generic retry/degraded-startup policy for active SecretRef provider failures to prevent supervisor restart storms?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but changing startup fail-closed behavior or adding retry/circuit-breaker/config surfaces affects credential security, service availability, operator diagnostics, and upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Add bounded generic retry/degrade policy
options.body: Implement a provider-agnostic startup policy that retries transient SecretRef provider failures briefly, then emits actionable diagnostics without provider-specific 1Password hardcoding.

options.title: Keep fail-fast and document supervisors
options.body: Preserve the current strict startup contract and add launchd/systemd restart-storm guidance plus external resolver/plugin recommendations.

options.title: Design broader lazy/degraded secrets model
options.body: Pause this issue behind a larger design for required versus optional SecretRef surfaces and first-use resolution semantics.

recommendation.title: Add bounded generic retry/degrade policy
recommendation.body: Implement a provider-agnostic startup policy that retries transient SecretRef provider failures briefly, then emits actionable diagnostics without provider-specific 1Password hardcoding.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue centers on the SecretRef runtime and provider-based external secrets behavior introduced in this area.
